text: Before we enter the landscape, meet the man behind the archive. Weston A. Price was a dentist whose journeys became a book, Nutrition and Physical Degeneration, published in 1939. Today, his photographs invite us to look again. At places. At people. And at the questions a picture leaves open.

text: Switzerland. The summer of 1931. Price visits the Loetschental Valley and returns to Switzerland the following year. Let your eye travel between the mountains and the village below. This is Figure One in his book. Our first doorway into a place, and the people who made a life here.

text: Now look beyond the roofs. Price describes land used for hay and rye, and forests protected against falling snow and rock. Read with his account, the landscape becomes a record of work and the seasons. These are his observations. A photograph offers one view; the people who lived here would have many more.

text: Across the world, another photograph opens. A wooden building. Two people at its entrance. And a name, painted on the wall: Rotorua Dental Clinic. This is Figure Sixty Eight in Price's book. Follow that name into the globe and you can explore Rotorua, then return to this very moment.

text: A small building belongs to a wider story. In April 1921, thirty women began training in Wellington for New Zealand's School Dental Service. The programme brought dental care to primary school children. That date marks the beginning of the training programme. The exact date of this photograph remains unconfirmed.

text: Come closer to the people at the door. Price identifies the man as Colonel Saunders, and the woman as a dental operator. He does not give her name in this passage.
